paper_type_evidence.quote: We have used the Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) mounted at the Very Large Telescope to characterize the GRB host galaxy.
In addition, we performed deep radio-continuum observations of the host with the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and with ALMA at 1.3 mm.

findings_qualitative.value: The GRB 050709 host galaxy is undetected in ALMA Band 6 (1.3 mm) and Spitzer 24 um, ruling out substantial optically obscured star formation.

evidence.quote: The galaxy is detected neither by ALMA nor by Spitzer , excluding a substantial amount of optically obscured star formation activity.

findings_qualitative.value: BPT diagrams, faint diffuse 5.5 GHz radio emission in excess of star formation, irregular optical morphology with a double peak and tidal tails, and smooth gas kinematics together indicate the host is in an advanced merger stage.

evidence.quote: This potential evidence for shocked gas, the very irregular morphological appearance of the host, and a comparison of the observed kinematics of the Hα-emitting gas with analogous results for merging field galaxies led us to conclude that the GRB 050709 host is most likely a galaxy in an advanced merger stage.

claims.hypothesis: The faint diffuse ATCA 5.5 GHz radio source in the eastern part of the GRB 050709 host galaxy is due to obscured star-forming activity (~2-3 M_sun yr^-1).
claims.experiment: Observe the host galaxy with ALMA in Band 6 (1.3 mm), analyze archival Spitzer 24 um imaging, and map extinction-corrected Halpha emission with VLT/MUSE.
claims.result: The host is undetected by ALMA (< 55 uJy beam^-1, SFR < 4.5 M_sun yr^-1, median template ~1.6 M_sun yr^-1) and Spitzer (< 34 uJy, SFR < 1.5 M_sun yr^-1), while the global extinction-corrected Halpha SFR is 0.15 ± 0.02 M_sun yr^-1.
claims.finding: Substantial optically obscured star formation is ruled out; the faint diffuse radio emission is in excess of pure star formation and likely arises from nonthermal processes such as shocked gas.

evidence.quote: The galaxy is detected neither by ALMA nor by Spitzer , excluding a substantial amount of optically obscured star formation activity.
The ATCA observations reveal faint diffuse radio emission at the eastern part of the host in excess to that expected from pure star formation, possibly further evidence for nonthermal processes.

If this faint radio component were due to star formation activity, this would correspond to an SFR of about 2–3 M ⊙ yr − 1 . However, in line with the ALMA and Spitzer non-detections, the MUSE observations do not support such an interpretation.

claims.hypothesis: The morphologically disturbed host galaxy of short GRB 050709 is a galaxy in an advanced merger stage.
claims.experiment: Inspect HST/F814W morphology and map spatially resolved ionized gas kinematics, metallicity, and BPT line ratios using VLT/MUSE.
claims.result: HST shows a double central peak separated by 0.30'' (0.85 kpc) and tidal tails; BPT diagrams show spaxels near the demarcation line and in the slow-shock regime; Halpha kinematics show a smooth velocity gradient and sigma_dyn,gas ~ 20-40 km s^-1 resembling type M4 advanced mergers.
claims.finding: The host of GRB 050709 is most likely a dwarf galaxy in an advanced merger stage.

evidence.loc: 2.2.2. The host seen by the HST
evidence.quote: Varying the contrast parameters in this image shows that the optically brightest region (labeled B) has two emission peaks (Fig. 1), possibly indicative of a tight pair of galaxies in an advanced merger stage.
A visual inspection of their Fig. 5 reveals three galaxies where the morphology and the kinematics of the interstellar gas strongly resemble the case of the GRB 050709 host.

This potential evidence for shocked gas, the very irregular morphological appearance of the host, and a comparison of the observed kinematics of the Hα-emitting gas with analogous results for merging field galaxies led us to conclude that the GRB 050709 host is most likely a galaxy in an advanced merger stage.

claims.hypothesis: Luminous late-time radio emission from the GRB afterglow or a kilonova radio flare is present ~8 years (6.93 yr rest frame) after short GRB 050709.
claims.experiment: Perform deep ATCA radio-continuum observations at 5.5 and 9.0 GHz 8.04 years post-burst.
claims.result: No point source is detected at the GRB position down to 3 sigma < 15 uJy (5 sigma < 25 uJy), corresponding to specific luminosities L_nu < (1.5-1.8) x 10^28 erg s^-1 Hz^-1.
claims.finding: Very luminous radio transients following double neutron star mergers either do not exist or do not peak years after the burst.

evidence.quote: At standard resolution (robust parameter = 0), there is no evidence for a source at the GRB position at either frequency ( F ν (5.5 GHz) < 15 µJy, F ν (9.0 GHz) < 15 µJy; 3σ).

evidence.loc: 5.3. Constraints on GRB late-time emission components
evidence.quote: It further supports the conclusion that very luminous radio transients following DNS mergers do not exist. Or, if they do exist, they do not peak years after the burst.

why_this_data.value: GRB 050709 is at z = 0.1606, making it one of the nearest short-GRB hosts and suitable for spatially resolved VLT/MUSE spectroscopy; ALMA Band 6 (and requested Band 9) observations were obtained to test whether the faint ATCA radio source is due to dust-obscured star formation.

evidence.quote: At a redshift of z = 0.16, it belongs to one of the cosmologically nearest short-GRB hosts identified to date. Consequently, it represents a promising target for sensitive, spatially resolved observational studies.

In order to clarify if the faint ATCA radio source is related to star-forming activity in the eastern part of the galaxy, we applied for ALMA observations in bands 6 (1.1–1.4 mm, 211–275 GHz) and 9 (0.4–0.5 mm, 602–720 GHz).

why_this_method.value: Used O3N2 and BPT line ratios because lines are close in wavelength and insensitive to dust extinction or instrumental response; used Briggs robust = 2.0 in ALMA and varied robust 0.0-2.0 in ATCA to maximize sensitivity.

evidence.quote: The Briggs “robust” parameter (Briggs 1995) was varied between 0.0 and 2.0 (natural weighting for maximum sensitivity).
Since the flux ratios refer to lines that are very close to each other, the line ratios are basically insensitive to extinction by dust along the line of sight or instrumental response.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Star-formation origin for the ATCA 5.5 GHz extended emission (rejected by ALMA, Spitzer, and MUSE SFR constraints in favor of nonthermal/shocked gas emission)

evidence.quote: Using Eq. (1) in Greiner et al. (2016), the observed 5.5 GHz flux would then correspond to an unobscured SFR in the eastern part of the host of ∼2−3 M ⊙ yr − 1 . However, our VLT/MUSE observations do not support this picture (Sect. 3.4).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: GRB radio afterglow or late-time kilonova radio flare origin for the ATCA 5.5 GHz extended emission (rejected because those sources would be < 1 mas and point-like)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Infall of external metal-poor gas clouds or stellar wind feedback as alternative explanations for the lower metallicity and higher SFR in region B

evidence.quote: If correct, this, in combination with the fact that the SFR peaks in region B (Fig. 5), could indicate that star formation is triggered here by the infall of metal-poor gas.

Feedback from stellar winds, which is especially efficient in the low potential well of low-mass galaxies, could be an alternative scenario because regions that have consumed their gas more quickly (and so have lower SFRs) have had a higher metal production rate

limitations_admitted.value: Scheduled ALMA Band 9 observations could not be performed due to weather constraints.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, due to weather constraints observations in band 9 could not be performed despite being scheduled.

limitations_admitted.value: The faint ATCA 5.5 GHz extended emission near the GRB site is at the ~5 sigma level, so there is no guarantee that it is real and it is too faint to split in time or frequency.

evidence.quote: We conclude that there may be some extended emission at the GRB explosion site at the 5σ level. This is too faint to perform a more detailed analysis (e.g., splitting in time or frequency). It does not look like a spurious source, but at the S/N level at which we detect it there is no guarantee that it is real.

limitations_admitted.value: Small angular sizes (< 0.2''), faintness, and strong host foreground emission prevent MUSE from clarifying the nature of individual clumps C-G and K-M.

evidence.loc: 4.1. The nature of objects C-G and K-M
evidence.quote: While the HST image seems to provide compelling evidence that these are star-forming regions, young luminous stellar clusters, or background (foreground) galaxies, their individual nature cannot be clarified with certainty using the MUSE data cube.

limitations_admitted.value: Low S/N in the outskirts of the galaxy prevents measuring E(B-V)_host, EW(Halpha), or a secure SFR at the GRB explosion site.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, there is no data point close to the GRB explosion site.

evidence.loc: 5.2. The GRB progenitor and the GRB explosion site
evidence.quote: Our data sensitivity is not good enough, however, to measure the corresponding SFR in this part of the galaxy with certainty.

limitations_admitted.value: Apparent lower metallicity in region B and high velocity dispersions (~60 km s^-1) in the outskirts could be affected by low-number statistics or low S/N.

evidence.quote: Region B appears to be less metal-rich than the outer parts of the galaxy, but we caution that such a conclusion could also be a result of low-number statistics (a small number of spaxels with data).
values of up to about 60 km s−1 occur at the outskirts of the galaxy, though we cannot rule out that this is due to a lower S/N.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA Band 6 combined image has a high angular resolution (0.22'' x 0.18''), which could resolve out diffuse dust continuum emission across the ~3-4'' host galaxy; a uv-tapered ALMA upper limit is not reported.
Setting E(B-V)_host = 0 for outer spaxels with low Hbeta S/N systematically underestimates the extinction-corrected SFR in the galaxy outskirts.

evidence.quote: A combined HST/F814W image (32 ks total exposure time) is provided by the Hubble Legacy Archive 3 .
